name: 192.com

search.notes: 192.com returned HTTP 403 to automated requests, so the site's own search URL pattern was not inspected. Use a search engine query restricted to 192.com, or open 192.com in a normal browser and search by name and town.

steps: Open the 192.com record removal request form in a normal browser.
Enter first name, surname, postcode and an email address the person can read. Up to five other people at the same address can be added.
Answer the human check on the form. The human must do this step.
Submit the form, then open the confirmation email from 192.com and click the link. The request is not processed until the link is clicked.
Keep the confirmation email as evidence.
Check 192.com again after a few days. If the record is still visible, reply to 192.com with the confirmation email and ask for the status in writing.
Also opt out of the open electoral register (see gb-open-register), because 192.com takes data from it and a record can come back at the next refresh.
optout.notes: The form URL and the 48 hour figure come from a third-party guide and could not be confirmed on 192.com today. A postal request using the C01 form is also possible and can take up to 28 days. Removal hides 192.com records only. It does not make a landline ex-directory and it does not remove data from the electoral register.

sources.attribution: Form URL and timelines as described in an Offlist guide. Not confirmed on 192.com.
Background on the C01 form and the open register source.

verification_note: 192.com, 192.com/c01/new-request/ and 192.com/help/ all returned HTTP 403 to curl and WebFetch on 2026-10-21. The form URL comes from a third-party guide only.
